title: Café Achteck Berlin - Quick Summary
kicker: WALK OF BERLIN • LIVING IN BERLIN
items: **What a Café Achteck is:** Berlin's green octagonal cast-iron street urinal, designed in **1878** by city councillor Carl Theodor Rospatt with seven standing stalls behind a privacy screen.
**How many existed vs today:** Around **142 units** stood across Greater Berlin by 1920; today **13 green octagons** still stand outdoors, and **11** remain in active toilet service.
**In service and free:** All **11 operating pavilions** are run by **Wall GmbH**, listed **24 hours a day**, and cost **0 euros** (none are wheelchair-accessible).
**Urinal-only vs all-gender:** Nine operated pavilions remain **men-only standing urinals**; two (**Rüdesheimer Platz** and **Fellbacher Platz**) were rebuilt with two seated cabins for everyone.
**Two you cannot pee in:** **Huttenstraße/Wiebestraße** in Moabit stands locked as a monument, and the pavilion at **Museum Reinickendorf** (Alt-Hermsdorf 35) is a museum info booth.
**Famous mix-ups:** The **Gendarmenmarkt** octagon was a 2003 replica removed in **2019**; **Schlesisches Tor** (Burgermeister) is a rectangular brick toilet house, not a Café Achteck.
**My move:** Open the survivor map below from the station you are leaving, or check live operating status in the free **Berliner Toilette** app.
